expected_mechanism.summary: Trigger arming completes, accel_init reports ready, and the work-handler registration (correctly guarded by CONFIG_ACCEL_TRIGGER_GLOBAL_THREAD) stays live - but the ONLY k_work_submit site for the registered work item is enclosed by the misspelled guard '#if defined(CONFIG_ACCEL_TRIGGER_GLOBAL_THREAAD)' (the Kconfig symbol is CONFIG_ACCEL_TRIGGER_GLOBAL_THREAD), so the submit is compiled out under every configuration: init/submit pairing inconsistent, deterministically, at source level.
expected_mechanism.determinism: source-deterministic: the branch is dead under every configuration, not merely under the pinned one

expected_predicates.statement: CONFIG_ACCEL_TRIGGER_GLOBAL_THREAD is the selected trigger mode (Kconfig choice default y; selects ACCEL_TRIGGER) in the pinned build context

the only k_work_submit call in the slice is enclosed by '#if defined(CONFIG_ACCEL_TRIGGER_GLOBAL_THREAAD)', a token that no Kconfig source in the slice defines (misspelling of CONFIG_ACCEL_TRIGGER_GLOBAL_THREAD), so the branch is not taken under any configuration
k_work_submit(&accel_work) is not reachable under the pinned build config: no live call edge reaches it, while the handler registration accel_work.handler = accel_work_cb is live
accel_work_cb and the work item accel_work are defined and registered; module readiness (accel_ready) is set unconditionally by accel_init regardless of the submit branch

two_part_separation.part_b_required_but_unavailable: runtime occurrence (whether the work item is ever queued/executed at runtime, and any runtime effect) is NOT a source-derived fact and must be recorded as required-but-unavailable

forbidden_overclaims: 'the work handler crashed at runtime' / 'NULL-handler crash at runtime'
any claim that the work item never executes at runtime (runtime semantics are out of scope; only the source-level pairing inconsistency is claimable)
